questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India affirms the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred in Part III of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Article 32 is known as the Right to Constitutional Remedies. It affirms the right of a citizen to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights (Part III). Dr. B.R. Ambedkar famously called this article the 'Heart and Soul' of the Constitution.

Note: Under this article, the Supreme Court can issue writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari.

questions.question: In 1959, the Central Government of India undertook the governance in Kerala under ______ of the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
In 1959, the Central Government dismissed the communist government in Kerala and imposed President's Rule under Article 356. This article allows the Union to take over the state administration if the Constitutional machinery fails.

Note: This was one of the first and most controversial instances of the use of Article 356 in independent India.

questions.question: When was the First Law Commission set up in independent India?
questions.solution:
The First Law Commission of independent India was established in 1955 for a three-year term. It was chaired by M. C. Setalvad, who was also the first Attorney General of India.

Additional Info: Law Commissions are non-statutory bodies constituted by the Government to recommend legislative reforms.

questions.question: What is the tenure of the chairman of the State Public Service Commission?
questions.option_1: 5 years or the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
questions.option_2: 6 years or the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
questions.option_3: 5 years or the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
questions.option_4: 6 years or the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
questions.solution:
The Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission (SPSC) hold office for a term of 6 years or until they reach the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.

Comparison: For the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), the age limit is 65 years. While the Governor appoints SPSC members, they can only be removed by the President.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) first constituted?
questions.solution:
The Council of States (Rajya Sabha) was first constituted on 3 April 1952. Its first session was held on 13 May 1952.

Historical Note: Until 1954, it was officially known as the 'Council of States' before the Hindi name 'Rajya Sabha' was adopted.

questions.question: How many members are nominated by the President in the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The President of India nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha. These members are selected from people who have special knowledge or practical experience in Literature, Science, Art, and Social Service.

Purpose: To allow distinguished persons to contribute to the legislature without going through the election process.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the functioning of Rajya Sabha is correct?
questions.option_1: Rajya Sabha is dissolved after the assent of the President of India.
questions.option_2: Rajya Sabha is dissolved every second year.
questions.option_3: Rajya Sabha is dissolved after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
questions.option_4: Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution.
questions.solution:
The Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution; it is a permanent body. However, one-third of its members retire every second year, and their seats are filled by fresh elections and presidential nominations.

Note: Each member is elected for a term of six years.

questions.question: In which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India is right to property mentioned?
questions.solution:
The Right to Property is currently mentioned in Article 300 A. Originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31, it was shifted to Part XII as a Legal Right by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

Key Note: This means the state can still take property, but it must follow the due process of law.

questions.question: Features of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution partly derives its inspiration from the Bill of Rights, enshrined in the Constitution of ______.
questions.solution:
The Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Bill of Rights of the United States of America. Part III (Articles 12-35) acts as a guarantee of civil liberties to all Indians.

Note: While inspired by the US, the Indian version includes more elaborate restrictions and specific provisions like the abolition of untouchability.

questions.question: When was the State Reorganisation Act passed by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The State Reorganisation Act was passed in 1956. This act was a major reform of the boundaries of India's states and territories, organising them largely along linguistic lines.

Result: It created 14 states and 6 union territories at that time.

questions.question: ______ is a draft of a legislative proposal before the House.
questions.solution:
A Bill is a draft of a legislative proposal presented in either House of Parliament. Once it is passed by both Houses and receives the President's assent, it becomes an Act.

Process: It goes through three readings in each house before being sent to the President.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Constitution of India mentions Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
Part III of the Constitution of India (Articles 12 to 35) contains the Fundamental Rights. These are often described as the Magna Carta of India.

Classification: They are grouped into six categories, such as Right to Equality and Right to Freedom.

questions.question: The members of the Constituent Assembly signed the Constitution of India on ______.
questions.solution:
The members of the Constituent Assembly signed the final Constitution of India on 24 January 1950. Two days later, on 26 January 1950, it officially came into effect.

Fact: 284 members actually signed the document on that day in the Constitution Hall.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India states that 'The President, or the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State, shall not be answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and duties of his office'?
questions.solution:
Article 361 provides immunity to the President and Governors. It states they are not answerable to any court for the exercise of their official powers and duties. Additionally, no criminal proceedings can be instituted against them during their term of office.

Purpose: To protect the dignity and independence of the highest constitutional offices.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Supreme Court of India come into existence after Independence?
questions.solution:
The Supreme Court of India came into existence on 28 January 1950, two days after India became a Sovereign Democratic Republic. It replaced the Federal Court of India and the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council.

Note: Its first proceedings were held in the Chamber of Princes in the Parliament building.

questions.question: The polity of a country is designed according to its ______ and any change to the polity is possible only when an amendment is made.
questions.solution:
The polity of a country is designed according to its Constitution. The Constitution is the supreme law of the land that defines the framework of government and the rights of citizens.

Note: Article 368 provides the power and procedure to amend this framework.

questions.question: ______ is a set of norms and guidelines to be followed by the political parties and contesting candidates during election time.
questions.solution:
The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) is a set of guidelines issued by the Election Commission of India for the conduct of political parties and candidates during elections. It kicks in as soon as the election schedule is announced.

Purpose: To ensure free and fair elections and prevent the misuse of power by the ruling party.

questions.question: Who among the following is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha. This means by virtue of holding the office of Vice-President, they automatically become the presiding officer of the Upper House.

Note: Unlike the Speaker of Lok Sabha, the Chairman is not a member of the House they preside over.

questions.question: Who among the following became the first Lokpal of India?
questions.solution:
Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became the first Lokpal of India in March 2019. The Lokpal is an anti-corruption authority or body of ombudsman who represents the public interest in the Republic of India.

Context: The appointment followed years of movements for the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act.

questions.question:
Which of the given Articles of the Constitution of India mentions the following?
"There shall be a council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President who shall in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice."
questions.solution:
Article 74(1) states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President. The President is generally bound to act in accordance with such advice.

Note: The 42nd and 44th Amendments clarified and slightly modified the binding nature of this advice.

questions.question: In which year did the Central Government of India appoint the States Reorganisation Commission?
questions.solution:
The States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) was appointed by the Central Government in 1953. It was headed by Fazal Ali and included H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members.

Outcome: Their recommendations led to the State Reorganisation Act of 1956.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India a Judge of the Supreme Court cannot be removed from office except by an order of the ______.
questions.solution:
A Judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only by an order of the President. This order is issued after an address by Parliament, supported by a special majority in each House, has been presented to the President in the same session.

Grounds: Removal is possible only on grounds of 'proved misbehaviour' or 'incapacity'.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry?
questions.solution:
Article 48 (a Directive Principle) directs the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines. It also mentions taking steps for preserving and improving breeds and prohibiting the slaughter of cows and calves.

Note: Article 48A (added later) deals with environment and wildlife.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to be an eligible voter for Lok Sabha elections?
questions.solution:
The minimum age to be an eligible voter in India is 18 years. This was changed from 21 years to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

Term: This principle is known as Universal Adult Franchise, mentioned under Article 326.
